Apple derives it algorithmically from inactive periods across the whole day, runs systematically higher than a seated reading, and lags a day — it is NOT comparable to the <55 baseline, which came from direct measurement. The 52 corroborates everything else in the session (best HR-for-pace in a fortnight, 70bpm at 2min post-run, 8s total in Zone 3+). The HR-governed defence holds while runs are short; at Week 4 (18km inside a 40km week) a 20sec/km Saturday overspeed is what breaks the Sunday.

THE KEY AEROBIC FINDING: HR climbed 117->129->132->132->134->135->136->138->143 through km9 then went COMPLETELY FLAT at 145/145/145 for km10-12 while pace held 5:29/5:28/5:27 and power held 218/221/218w. He found steady state and locked onto it in the final third of the longest run he has ever done — the aerobic system was not being progressively overwhelmed. That is precisely the quality a half marathon asks for. Pw:HR DECOUPLING 4.3% (first-half EF 209w/129.8bpm = 1.610; second-half 218.8w/142bpm = 1.541) — under the 5% threshold for well-developed aerobic endurance at this duration. COUNTERWEIGHT: km4 and km12 were both 5:27/km at ~217w but 13bpm apart (132 vs 145) — real drift across 40min, though most is the normal warm-up curve (km4 had not reached steady state) and the decisive point is that it FLATTENED rather than ran away. vs 7 Jun (previous longest, 11km): km4 5:27 @ 132bpm/216w vs 7 Jun's 5:27 @ 136bpm/219w = same pace 4bpm lower; km10 5:29 @ 145bpm/218w vs 7 Jun's 5:38 @ 145bpm/213w = 9sec/km FASTER at identical HR. Modest but real improvement, and it sits at the BACK END of the run where it matters. ZONE CONTROL: 99.1% Zone 1-2, only 0:59 above 150; the <150 cap exceeded by 2bpm at the very end = ordinary cardiac drift. Post-workout 138->98->90 = 40bpm drop in the first minute after 67 minutes running. Resting HR 52 (seated TICKR), SECOND consecutive reading — baseline confirmed, Apple daily 63 dismissed. Sleep 6-7h/1 wake — under the 8h optimal but immaterial for an aerobic session. CAUTION FOR THE LONGER RUNS: this was negative-split, drifting 5:39 -> 5:27. Fine over 12km. Over 16 and 18km hold 5:40 rather than letting it creep — the last 3km should be a choice, not a consequence. Week 1 complete: ~24.5km across 3 runs + 2 Barry's, on plan.
